# Reflecting instruments (octant, sextant) (`reflecting_octant_sextant`)

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from techtree/core/navigation.yaml — do not edit -->

- Category: Navigation, transport & exploration (`navigation`)
- Deps: helped by glass_mirrors, latitude_astrolabe_quadrant, telescope
- Core idea: Two mirrors bring the image of a star or the Sun down onto the horizon, so both are seen at once and the observer can judge coincidence despite the ship's motion; an angle doubles on the scale (a 60° arc measures 120°), and with a small telescope altitudes are good to a minute of arc.
- Pitfalls:
  - Measuring the Sun without shade glasses (eye damage)
  - Proposing it in 1490 as a ready tool: instruments accurate to about a minute of arc are more than 250 years away
- History: europe: 1731 – John Hadley's octant (also Thomas Godfrey, Philadelphia); 1757 Campbell's sextant
- Read:
  - John Hadley, The Description of a New Instrument for Taking Angles, Philosophical Transactions 37 (1731)
  - Derek Howse, Greenwich Time and the Discovery of the Longitude (1980)
